chunks: From him, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the hunting of the falcon and the hawk. He said, 'Do not eat what the falcon and the hawk kill, and do not eat what the birds of prey kill.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game caught by falcons and hawks in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between birds of prey that kill with their claws (like falcons and hawks) and those that kill with their beaks, ruling that prey killed by the former is not permissible to eat unless slaughtered properly. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the method of killing, contrasting with some Sunni schools that permit game caught by trained hunting dogs or birds of prey. The narration underscores the importance of ensuring the animal is slaughtered in accordance with Islamic rites rather than merely killed by the predator.
